title: Article 139 — Conferment on the Supreme Court of powers to issue certain writs

content.overview: Article 139 provides that Parliament may by law confer on the Supreme Court power to issue directions, orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, or any of them, for any purposes other than those mentioned in clause (2) of Article 32.
content.glance: Parliament may by law give SC writ powers for purposes other than Art 32(2) (enforcement of Part III rights).
content.study:
Article 32(2) already empowers the SC to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Article 139 allows Parliament to confer additional writ-issuing power on the SC for other purposes.

Examination: parliamentary conferment; purposes beyond Art 32(2); same five writs named.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Parliament may by law confer on the SC power to issue directions, orders or writs (including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, certiorari) for purposes other than those in Article 32(2).

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 139 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 139 provides that Parliament may by law confer on the Supreme Court power to issue directions, orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari, or any of them, for any purposes other than those mentioned in Article 32(2).

examTips: Parliament may enlarge SC writ power beyond FR enforcement.

keyTakeaways: Art 139: parliamentary power to confer additional SC writ jurisdiction.
